architecture.refresh_strategy: Acquire immutable, content-addressed source envelopes outside the public projection; build only from a frozen snapshot; use the governed artefact-dependency graph to select affected gates but fail closed where evidence cannot be carried forward; execute the pinned OKF Explorer consumer contract before publication; publish later observations as a new snapshot rather than backpatching release bytes.
architecture.scale_assumptions: At least 1,866 GOV.UK records plus up to 289 public repositories, 15 CDDO API rows, approximately 14 dataset records and control concepts; use lazy, integrity-bound Explorer overview, chunk, search, locator and adjacency entrypoints with bounded result rendering.

decision_authorities: The project owner approves scope, profile and release decisions.
HM Land Registry and relevant rights holders alone can determine source access, licence and official interpretation.
operational_authorities: Publisher-operated service pages, developer packs, terms and status notices define current operation.
The repository maintainer controls only the derived static publication and its release state.
semantic_authorities: Source-native HMLR definitions, identifiers, exclusions and version semantics take precedence over local normalisation.
Current legislation and formal notices outrank older service matrices, roadmaps and catalogue summaries.
Publisher-operated dataset pages outrank discovery catalogues for cadence, access and operational status.
The pinned OKF Bundle Wiki profile governs semantic serialisation, registries and assertion shape without becoming authority for HMLR facts.
The declared frozen metadata fields and approved deterministic rules are the only authority for generated relationship assertions; Reader projections are not an independent semantic source.
source_authorities: HM Land Registry is authoritative for its current formal guidance, services, datasets and operational documentation.
Legislation.gov.uk is authoritative for enacted legislation and official revised text.
Government Digital Service is authoritative for GOV.UK Search and Content API metadata.
Repository owners and dataset licensors are authoritative for their own licences and access terms.

acceptance_gates: The domain profile validates, JSON and YAML are equivalent, and the pack root digest is recorded.
The tiny positive, negative and degraded fixture builds twice with byte-identical output and fails closed.
Every expected source item has one terminal acquisition outcome and all envelopes rehash.
OKF core, canonical YAML-LD, equivalent JSON-LD, semantic registries, manifests, routes, counts, rights and source ledgers validate.
Every material directed relationship reconciles across its direct triple, evidence-bearing assertion and bounded Reader runtime row.
The inference state is explicit: not-run, or materialised only from an allowlisted finite rule manifest with complete supporting assertions.
The 24-question first-release suite has complete persona/story/source traceability and zero hard failures.
Accessibility, safety, performance and clean reproduction receipts bind the exact frozen candidate.
No public-release or completeness claim is made beyond owner-approved, digest-bound evidence.
build_recommendation.canonical_fixture: Include a current OGL dataset, bespoke-licensed dataset, restricted service, stale catalogue/current publisher pair, indicative spatial product, Welsh route, missing-rights repository, unsafe signed URL, duplicate identifier, unanswerable query and source-content prompt injection treated only as data.
deferred_features: Property-level, title, address, polygon or transaction data
Authenticated provider calls, live search and credential handling
Remote-context resolution, unbounded RDF, RDFS or OWL inference and browser-side reasoning
Turtle export and general-purpose SHACL or OWL entailment beyond the pinned Bundle Wiki validation profile
Federation until independently governed source lanes require separate releases
required_features: Frozen source envelopes with exact per-family denominators and terminal outcomes
Stable source-native identity, deterministic local routes and collision failure
Canonical YAML-LD and deterministic JSON-LD generated from one governed semantic assertion source using pinned local contexts
Digest-bound semantic-model, IRI-to-route and predicate registries with closed reference validation

Evidence-bearing catalogue, primary-topic, publisher, rights, provenance, translation, collection, distribution, documentation, service/dataset, version and replacement relationships when frozen metadata supports them
Exact direct-triple, reified-assertion and Reader-runtime parity with bounded relationship delivery
An explicit no-unbounded-inference policy and digest-bound rule manifest for any future materialised bounded inference
Search, source/type/access/topic facets and bounded result rendering
Record detail with authority, derivation, freshness, rights, coverage and caveats
Dataset distributions, API protocol/access and spatial boundary semantics
Persona/story/question traceability and direct-source evaluation baseline
Accessible, progressively enhanced GitHub Pages site and raw machine entrypoints

collection_profile.duplicate_policy: Preserve source-native routes and identifiers; relate alternate representations without collapsing documents, datasets, distributions, services or versions.
extraction_constraints: Metadata only from public, bounded routes.
Do not follow signed download URLs or store credentials.
Do not automate services whose terms prohibit automated agents.
Bound response size, redirects and pagination; reject unsafe URLs.
formats: PDF, ODT and ODS metadata only
languages: cy where an official Welsh representation is linked
representation_relationships: A GOV.UK route may have HTML, Welsh, attachment and Content API representations.
A dataset may have landing page, technical specification, full, delta, API and linked-data distributions.
A Business Gateway product may have documentation, schema, WSDL, test and production endpoints.
sensitivity_findings: Land-register information can contain personal information even when statutory access exists.
Corporate and Price Paid datasets contain third-party address rights.
Public forum content can expose personal or sensitive information.
Property searches and title products have legal and financial consequences.

constraints.effect: Business Gateway, portal, property services and some dataset APIs require accounts, approval, payment, keys or certificates.

constraints.effect: Register information, property results and forum content can contain personal or sensitive information.

constraints.effect: Fees, service state, local-authority migration, datasets and GOV.UK content change on different cadences.
constraints.mitigation: Snapshot every source, expose observed and source dates separately, and require live revalidation before action.

constraints.effect: The catalogue exceeds a small-bundle payload and source distributions can be multi-gigabyte.
constraints.mitigation: Lazy metadata shards, bounded search, no production data files and explicit performance budgets.

description: A snapshot-bounded, metadata-led and fully governed semantic profile for discovering HM Land Registry guidance, forms, services, datasets, APIs, developer resources and public repositories through evidence-bearing directed relationships without replacing authoritative sources, performing legal inference or redistributing restricted property data.

enrichment.authority_boundary: Derived metadata never becomes an official HMLR statement.
enrichment.budget: No paid model or API calls are authorised.
enrichment.evidence_requirement: Every non-source-native field and relationship names its frozen source artefact, source field or supporting assertion, deterministic method, observation and applicable rights.
enrichment.independent_review: Domain, semantic and rights assertions require review independent of the generating implementation before release; the 2026-08-10 owner direction is not that review.
enrichment.purpose: The full metadata-level semantic graph is authorised, but AI-assisted authoring does not authorise model-generated corpus assertions; published entities and relationships remain source-native, deterministically normalised or explicitly rule-derived.

baselines: Direct navigation and search on the named official source.
Deterministic lexical search over the frozen normalised catalogue.
evaluation.challenge_policy: Use two disjoint held-out passes containing stale, conflicting, similarly named, restricted, unanswerable and unsafe cases; publish new critical categories rather than averaging them away.
evaluation.citation_policy: Every material proposition must cite the exact publisher route or frozen source envelope; discovery catalogues cannot establish current operational status alone.

hard_failures: Legal, ownership, priority or exact-boundary advice is presented as a bundle conclusion.
A restricted, bespoke or unknown right is presented as OGL or unrestricted.
Catalogue modification time is presented as dataset release, validity or coverage.
A restricted service is called, monitored or presented as an anonymous public API.
A credential, signed download URL, personal-level record or forum upload enters the public bundle.
A result cannot resolve its authoritative source and observation.
Unknown, candidate or untested evidence is relabelled verified.
A material directed relationship lacks a governed predicate, route-bearing endpoints, field-level evidence, rights, authority, derivation or observation.
Direct triples, reified assertions, semantic shards, registries and Reader runtime relationships do not reconcile to the same exact identity set.
Unbounded inference, remote-context reasoning or an undeclared inferred or model-derived plane is enabled.
evaluation.independent_verification: The 24-question v0.2.0 suite was reviewed by an AI agent independent of the retrieval implementation against the frozen snapshot; this is not human domain assurance or participant research. The new semantic competency question and complete v0.3.0 relationship set are candidate inputs; only version-scoped evidence bound to the exact digest records their independent-review state.

desired_outcomes: People and agents can find the authoritative route for a land-registration task.
Data users can compare datasets by coverage, cadence, format, access and licence.
Property professionals and developers can distinguish public guidance from restricted operational services.
Every discovery result exposes its source, observation date, authority role and material caveats.
People and agents can traverse governed, evidence-bearing metadata relationships without mistaking the derived graph for legal advice or an HM Land Registry ontology.
non_goals: The bundle will not provide legal advice or determine ownership, boundaries or priority.
The bundle will not contain title-register, title-plan, search-result or bulk property records.
The bundle will not authenticate to, automate or monitor restricted HM Land Registry services.
The bundle will not claim completeness outside a named, dated denominator.
The bundle and Reader will not perform unbounded semantic inference or infer legal, ownership, boundary, priority, rights, authority, currency, coverage or identity conclusions.
intent.problem: HM Land Registry material is spread across GOV.UK, publisher-operated data and transaction services, developer documentation, linked data, help systems, GitHub and an official blog, with materially different authority, freshness, access and reuse conditions.

semantic_model.equivalence_policy: Do not assert identity from title, URL similarity, shared title number, address, hierarchy or embedding similarity.

identifier_policy.collision_rule: Fail closed on identity collision; never add numeric suffixes silently.
identifier_policy.iri_rule: Mint only repository-controlled derived IRIs, retain the canonical source URL separately and register every assertion endpoint IRI with exactly one safe local Reader route.
identifier_policy.native_identifier_rule: Preserve source routes, slugs, content IDs, service versions and repository full names verbatim.
identifier_policy.redirect_rule: Preserve source redirects and explicit replacement evidence; do not guess moved routes.
identifier_policy.route_rule: Use deterministic lower-case percent-safe routes prefixed by source family or semantic node kind; record every route, alias and collision in the digest-bound IRI-to-route registry.

identifier_schemes.collision_policy: Fail closed when two source identities map to one local route.
identifier_schemes.equivalence_policy: A redirect or similar title does not establish identity without source evidence.
identifier_schemes.normalization: Preserve native values and add a deterministic route-safe local identifier.
identifier_schemes.persistence: Routes can redirect; content identifiers are preferred when present.
identifier_schemes.scope: GOV.UK records attributed to HM Land Registry
identifier_schemes.syntax: Canonical GOV.UK route and source content identifier where supplied.

identifier_schemes.collision_policy: Fail closed on duplicate canonical URLs or slugs within one source.
identifier_schemes.equivalence_policy: Related fields or titles do not make two datasets identical.
identifier_schemes.normalization: Keep source slug and full canonical URL.
identifier_schemes.persistence: Preserve renamed legacy slugs as aliases, not replacement identities.
identifier_schemes.syntax: Canonical publisher URL and dataset slug.
identifier_schemes.uri_policy: Mint local IRIs from source kind and slug while retaining canonical source URL.

identifier_schemes.collision_policy: Fail closed on duplicate repository IDs or normalised names.
identifier_schemes.equivalence_policy: Fork, archive or successor relationships are not owl:sameAs.
identifier_schemes.normalization: Case-preserving full_name plus case-insensitive collision check.
identifier_schemes.persistence: Renames and transfers require explicit source metadata.
identifier_schemes.uri_policy: Use the GitHub html_url as source identity and a local derived IRI.

identifier_schemes.collision_policy: Fail closed if two canonical inputs, node kinds or assertion triples produce one IRI or if one IRI maps to more than one Reader route.
identifier_schemes.equivalence_policy: A shared source, publisher, rights statement, route label or graph neighbourhood does not establish entity identity.
identifier_schemes.issuer: HM Land Registry public-estate OKF project
identifier_schemes.normalization: Canonicalise only the reviewed identity fields for each node kind; hash canonical UTF-8 values where no stable source identifier exists.
identifier_schemes.persistence: Retain stable IRIs while the canonical source identity and derivation rule are unchanged; issue a new IRI for a materially different entity or assertion.
identifier_schemes.scope: Derived catalogue, catalogue-record, collection, distribution, publisher, rights, activity, evidence and relationship-assertion nodes
identifier_schemes.syntax: Repository-controlled HTTPS IRI under /id/<kind>/ and a separately validated local Reader route.
identifier_schemes.uri_policy: Record every absolute IRI and safe local route in the digest-bound IRI-to-route registry; neither value is inferred from display text.

prohibited_inferences: Do not infer legal ownership, exact boundary or priority from discovery metadata.
Do not infer beneficial ownership from corporate proprietor data.
Do not infer open reuse from public or free access.
Do not infer dataset currency from catalogue modification.
Do not infer nationwide LLC coverage from service availability.
Do not use owl:sameAs without authoritative identity evidence.
Do not infer a domain predicate from a Markdown link, presentation group, search facet, shared topic, co-occurrence, graph proximity, title similarity, URL similarity or embedding similarity.
Do not infer domain or range membership, transitive closure, inverse edges or replacement from vocabulary declarations alone.
Do not infer official authority, evidential support or rights from another relationship, a high confidence score or public availability.
Do not resolve arbitrary remote contexts or run unbounded RDF, RDFS or OWL reasoning in the build or Reader.
Do not mix a materialised inferred or model-derived plane into the official or normalised default planes.

relationship_types.label: is part of

relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Membership explicitly observed or deterministically generated for the frozen candidate.

relationship_types.label: has part
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Source-declared collection membership or a publisher distribution listing with both endpoint identities preserved.
non_properties: A hyperlink alone is not membership.
A dataset and one of its distributions are not identical.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: True for the observed source snapshot.

relationship_types.label: has distribution
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Publisher-declared distribution identity, kind, format and dataset membership in the frozen metadata.
non_properties: A format label without a distinct distribution identity is not a distribution node.
Do not retain credentials or signed download URLs as identities.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Distribution membership as declared for the observed dataset release or landing page.

relationship_types.label: has access service
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher metadata linking a distribution to a named service with its access model retained.
non_properties: A documentation URL or API example does not establish anonymous operational access.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Access-service association observed in publisher metadata at snapshot time.

relationship_types.label: serves dataset
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher API or service documentation naming the dataset and service identities.
non_properties: Shared title text or a catalogue provider field does not establish this relationship.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Service-to-dataset association observed in the frozen publisher documentation.

relationship_types.label: has documentation page
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher documentation link naming both the documented object and documentation work.
non_properties: Documentation does not imply public operation, service availability, current status or reuse rights.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Documentation relationship explicitly observed at snapshot time.

relationship_types.label: is translation of work
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Frozen GOV.UK Content API available_translations metadata with shared content identity, locale and exact source-value digest.
non_properties: A language tag, similar title or cross-link alone is not translation evidence.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Translation relationship declared by GOV.UK at the bounded Content API observation time.

relationship_types.label: is version of
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher edition, release, schema-version, commit or version relationship with stable identities for both endpoints.
non_properties: A later date, matching title or mutable route alone does not establish a version relationship.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Source-declared version relationship applicable to the observed release or edition.

relationship_types.label: supersedes
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher replacement, redirect or formal notice.
non_properties: Newer publication date alone does not prove supersession.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Replacement applies from the source-stated date.

relationship_types.cardinality: exactly one current publisher relationship per published discovery object, unless the source explicitly declares joint publishers
relationship_types.label: is published by
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Source-native publisher or organisation attribution from the frozen source, retaining authority role separately.
non_properties: Publisher attribution does not imply official endorsement of the derived catalogue or ownership of third-party rights.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Publisher role observed in the frozen source metadata.

relationship_types.cardinality: one or more applicable rights relationships per published object or assertion
relationship_types.label: has rights statement
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Exact current applicable rights-assessment ID plus publisher terms evidence and source-layer classification.
non_properties: The relationship does not assert that source data is open, free of third-party rights or licensed under the project licence.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Rights assessment applicable to the represented source layer and observation.

relationship_types.cardinality: one or more for every deterministically derived record, entity or assertion
relationship_types.label: was derived from
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Content-addressed frozen source artefact and field or locator, with source and canonical value digests where a field value is normalised.
non_properties: Derivation does not upgrade project-authored metadata to official authority.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Derivation from the exact frozen source artefact used for this candidate.

relationship_types.cardinality: exactly one controlling generation activity for every generated record, node or assertion
relationship_types.label: was generated by
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Deterministic activity identity bound to the rule or tool version, frozen input digest and observation or generation time.
non_properties: A generation activity is not a source publisher action, external review or release approval.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Generation activity for the exact candidate bytes.

relationship_types.label: conforms to
relationship_types.minimum_evidence: Explicit publisher-declared schema, protocol or standard version; project-profile conformance additionally requires a passing exact-candidate validation receipt.
non_properties: Use of a file format, namespace or vocabulary term alone does not establish conformance.
relationship_types.temporal_meaning: Conformance claimed or verified for the named source or candidate version only.

standards.title: INSPIRE Data Specification on Cadastral Parcels
standards.validation: Check declared GML, CRS, identifier, cadence and attribution fields against publisher evidence.

standards.conformance_artifact: Source-format declaration only; no geometry is generated.
standards.title: Geography Markup Language
standards.validation: Match publisher-declared format and technical guidance.

terms_adopted: Level A and AA success criteria
standards.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines

tasks.authority_requirement: Current GOV.UK and HMLR service evidence.
consequences_of_error: Legal or financial reliance on the wrong product
tasks.freshness_tolerance: Revalidate at time of action; fees and service state are volatile.
tasks.goal: Find the authoritative service or guidance route and understand its product, cost and evidential limits.
hard_failures: The bundle states or implies ownership
an exact boundary or legal advice.
tasks.success: The user reaches the official route with the material warning visible before action.

tasks.authority_requirement: Formal current guidance and notices outrank older summaries.
tasks.goal: Find the current practice guide, form, fee, notice and digital route for a registration task.
hard_failures: An obsolete or superseded route is labelled current without warning.
likely_confusions: Older portal guidance versus current DRS coverage
tasks.success: The result exposes the formal source, date and related alternatives.

tasks.freshness_tolerance: Snapshot metadata may guide discovery; live publisher state must be checked before reuse.
tasks.goal: Select a dataset by purpose, coverage, cadence, format, licence and access model.
hard_failures: A mixed or bespoke licence is flattened to OGL
or catalogue dates are labelled as data currency.
tasks.success: The user can compare material differences and open the canonical publisher source.

tasks.authority_requirement: HMLR dataset technical guidance and product terms.
tasks.context: INSPIRE, National Polygon and title-plan discovery.
tasks.freshness_tolerance: Monthly snapshot with visible release date.
tasks.goal: Find the appropriate spatial product and interpret its coverage, CRS and boundary meaning safely.
hard_failures: The bundle calls an indicative polygon an exact legal boundary.
tasks.success: The product is discoverable with a non-map explanation and explicit limitation.

tasks.authority_requirement: Current publisher documentation and formal service notice.
tasks.context: Business Gateway, dataset API and linked-data integration.
tasks.goal: Identify the correct machine interface, contract, environment and onboarding requirement.
hard_failures: A credential is stored
or a restricted service is described as anonymous.
tasks.success: A developer reaches the official contract without the bundle attempting execution.

tasks.authority_requirement: Current programme page, service terms and PG79.
consequences_of_error: Incomplete conveyancing search or wrong authority process
tasks.freshness_tolerance: Revalidate at time of search or migration action.
tasks.goal: Determine the Local Land Charges route, migration coverage and boundary with CON29.
hard_failures: The bundle claims nationwide coverage or automates the restricted search service.
likely_confusions: Land Charges versus Local Land Charges
tasks.success: The user can identify the official route and visible scope boundary.

tasks.authority_requirement: Machine-readable provenance plus direct publisher evidence.
tasks.freshness_tolerance: Bound to the frozen snapshot and candidate digest.
tasks.goal: Verify source authority, derivation, freshness, rights, coverage and accessibility claims.
hard_failures: An unknown or untested state is relabelled passed.
tasks.success: Every sampled claim resolves to evidence and unsupported claims fail closed.

terminology.definition: HM Land Registry reference for an individual registered estate in land.
terminology.source_scope: HM Land Registry register and data products

terminology.definition: A representation of general position or indicative extent that does not by itself establish an exact legal boundary.
An HMLR-issued copy with an evidential role distinct from an online downloaded information copy.
A restriction or prohibition registered through the Local Land Charges regime for an in-scope authority.
terminology.owner: HM Land Registry and originating authorities

terminology.definition: Property sales in England and Wales sold for value and lodged for registration, subject to stated exclusions and lag.
terminology.source_scope: HM Land Registry Price Paid Data

terminology.definition: A collaborative UK index of changes in residential property values whose recent estimates can be provisional and revised.
terminology.owner: HM Land Registry and UK HPI partners

terminology.definition: A date describing a discovery record, not necessarily the underlying dataset release, validity or coverage.
terminology.source_scope: GOV.UK, CDDO, NDL and other catalogues

title: HM Land Registry public-estate domain profile

traceability.intent_or_requirement: Find authoritative HMLR material across the public estate.
Keep source authority, derivation, freshness, availability and release state distinct.
Publish a comprehensive metadata-level semantic graph with canonical YAML-LD, equivalent JSON-LD, closed registries, evidence-bearing directed relationships and no unbounded inference.
Preserve mixed dataset and service rights without unsafe acquisition.
Provide evidence-led personas, stories and evaluation coverage.
Publish a durable, accessible GitHub Pages discovery site.
Avoid legal overclaim, secrets, personal data and restricted-service automation.

users.authority_requirement: Must reach current official guidance and understand when legal representation or an official copy is needed.
users.context: Finding trustworthy information without routine professional access.
needs: Find the right property-information, registration, correction or fraud-prevention route.
Understand product cost, coverage and evidential status.
risks: Treating general information as legal advice.
Treating a downloaded register or indicative plan as official proof or an exact boundary.
users.role: Member of the public, property owner, buyer or seller

users.authority_requirement: Current practice guide, form, fee, notice and digital-service guidance must be distinguishable by date and authority.
needs: Find the applicable practice guide, form, fee and digital route.
Check processing, requisition, application and expedite guidance.
risks: Using an obsolete form, fee or portal workflow.
Mistaking an aggregate processing estimate for an application guarantee.

accessibility_language_needs: Clear comparison tables and exportable metadata
users.authority_requirement: Product scope, access agreement, fees and current service documentation must remain explicit.
users.context: Using HMLR lender and commercial services.
needs: Find charge, data-sync, portfolio and polygon services.
Distinguish guidance, portal functions and machine interfaces.
risks: Assuming a discovery record grants service access or data-reuse rights.
users.role: Lender, portfolio manager or mortgage-service user

users.authority_requirement: Dataset scope, exclusions, cadence, format, licence, attribution and quality caveats must come from publisher sources.
users.context: Selecting public or licensed land and property data for analysis.
needs: Compare PPD, UK HPI, ownership, transaction, requisition and spatial datasets.
Inspect source-native identifiers, CRS, temporal coverage and distribution types.
risks: Treating latest-month PPD or provisional UK HPI as complete or final.
Treating an index polygon as a legal boundary.
Redistributing bespoke-licensed or third-party address data.
users.role: Data analyst, researcher, journalist or GIS specialist

users.authority_requirement: Current publisher documentation, protocol, schema version, environment and authentication requirements must be inspectable.
users.context: Evaluating HMLR APIs and integration contracts.
needs: Find the correct Business Gateway, ULPD or linked-data interface.
Distinguish REST, SOAP/WSDL, test, production, public and restricted access.
risks: Copying stale catalogue endpoints or example dates as current facts.
Exposing credentials or signed download URLs.

users.authority_requirement: Current migration table, formal guidance, fees and supplier/API boundaries must be visible.
users.context: Migration, maintenance and search responsibilities across changing coverage.
needs: Determine whether an authority has migrated and which HMLR process applies.
Find originating-authority guidance and service boundaries.
risks: Treating LLC search as a replacement for CON29 enquiries.
users.role: Local-authority or originating-authority Local Land Charges officer

users.authority_requirement: Every claim needs source, observation, derivation, rights and release state.
users.context: Checking whether the derived catalogue makes supportable claims.
needs: Trace a normalised record to publisher evidence.
Identify unknown, restricted, stale, partial and unverified states.
risks: Automated checks being presented as legal, statistical or accessibility assurance.
users.role: Provenance, licensing, accessibility or service assessor

validation.method: Validate JSON and YAML against okf-domain-profile.v1, references and canonical equivalence.

Validate reserved files, concept types, actors, provenance and lifecycle.
Validate schemas, safe paths, stable routes, referential integrity, counts, chunk bounds and checksums.
validation.target: Explorer descriptor, manifest, records, search and relationships

validation.method: Require per-record access and rights states; scan for credentials, signed URLs, personal data and forbidden source layers.
Check question-to-story-to-persona traceability, direct-source expectations, retrieval metrics and hard failures.
Static semantic checks plus keyboard, focus, reflow, contrast and no-JavaScript browser journeys.
Build twice from the same frozen inputs and compare every generated byte and checksum.

Execute a tiny fixture and the exact candidate in the pinned OKF Explorer; require load, search, facet, detail, resource, relationship and deep-link journeys without console or resource failures; repeat the canonical deep link after deployment.

validation.method: Safe-parse canonical YAML-LD; prove exact JSON-LD data equivalence; expand only pinned local contexts; validate the semantic-model, IRI-to-route and predicate registries; validate every relationship assertion; reconcile the exact direct-triple, reified-assertion and Reader-runtime sets; verify evidence, rights, route and digest closure; and require inference to be not-run or finite, rule-manifest-bound and separately materialised.
validation.target: Canonical semantic graph, registries, relationship assertions, inference state and bounded Reader projection
validation.validator: scripts/check_bundle.py, tests/test_jsonld.py and the pinned OKF Explorer repository reconciler

validation.method: Validate the artefact-dependency graph, classify changed paths, select transitive outputs, consumers and gates, and fail closed on unknown or generated-only changes.
validation.target: Authored inputs, generated outputs, consumer contracts and release gates
